close_reason: Handler-side enforcement done in commit c5aac30 with two regression tests. The handler now hoists a get_objects fetch and rejects sequential / intra-batch duplicates via alreadyExists. The backend-side concurrent-write race protection is tracked separately as JMAP-x2gd.101.
description:
Site:
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/position.rs:5-7 (doc comment): 'There is at most one ReadPosition per (account, chat) pair. Create and destroy are supported (unlike singletons), but each chat's read position is unique — backends must enforce the (account, chatId) uniqueness constraint.'
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/position.rs:144-198 (handle_position_set create): no uniqueness check; just calls create_object<ReadPosition>.
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:681-714 (generic create_object): no uniqueness check by (chatId).

Doc says 'backends must enforce' — MemoryBackend does not. A client calling ReadPosition/set create twice with the same chatId gets two ReadPosition records. Subsequent ReadPosition/get for that chat returns both; subsequent ReadPosition/set updates only one (whichever the chosen id picks), leaving the other stale; subsequent Chat.unreadCount derivation (per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Chat unreadCount line 485-486) is ambiguous.

This is the kind of bug that is invisible in tests (none create duplicates) and shows up in production when client retries land twice.

Fix sketch:
1. In handle_position_set create, look up existing ReadPositions by chatId before creating. If one exists, return alreadyExists pointing at the canonical id (the Chat/set Direct create pattern at chat.rs:181-194 is the model).
2. AND in MemoryBackend.create_object<ReadPosition>, enforce the uniqueness atomically (the kit's policy is backend-canonical; without backend enforcement, two concurrent creates can both pass the handler's pre-check).

Tests should cover: two sequential creates for same chatId → second yields alreadyExists; two concurrent creates → at most one succeeds.
title: ReadPosition uniqueness invariant 'one per (account, chat)' is unenforced; duplicate creates silently succeed
